_**Agent (claude-4.6-sonnet-medium-thinking)**_

Here is a thorough summary of everything found in the codebase:

---

## 1. Components/Pages Related to "Upgrades", "Latest-Versions", or "Archetypes"

There is **no dedicated page** for upgrades or latest-versions. The upgrade concept exists only as a toggleable feature flag. Archetypes appear in two pages:

**`src/pages/QualityReports.tsx`** — displays `archetype` and `archetypeVersion` in both the table and the detail dialog.

**`src/pages/ReviewMetrics.tsx`** — same pattern: displays `archetype` and `archetypeVersion` in the table and detail dialog.

**`src/pages/RepoSettings.tsx`** — exposes `upgradeEnabled` as a toggle labeled "Dependency Upgrades" in the repo editor.

There is no `/upgrades` route in `applicationMenu.tsx` or anywhere else in the routing.

---

## 2. How Versions Are Currently Displayed in the UI

Versions (`archetypeVersion`) are displayed as plain text strings, with no color coding, badges, or comparison indicators. They fall back to a dash (`—`) when absent.

In the **table rows** of both `QualityReports.tsx` and `ReviewMetrics.tsx`:

```125:129:src/pages/QualityReports.tsx
<td className="px-4 py-3 text-[var(--color-fonts-font-color-support)]">
  {row.repo.archetype ?? '—'}
</td>
<td className="px-4 py-3 text-[var(--color-fonts-font-color-support)]">
  {row.repo.archetypeVersion ?? '—'}
</td>
```

In the **detail dialog header** (same pattern in both pages):

```300:308:src/pages/QualityReports.tsx
{repo.archetype && (
  <span className="text-xs text-[var(--color-fonts-font-color-support)]">
    Archetype: <span className="font-medium text-[var(--color-fonts-font-color-primary)]">{repo.archetype}</span>
  </span>
)}
{repo.archetypeVersion && (
  <span className="text-xs text-[var(--color-fonts-font-color-support)]">
    Version: <span className="font-medium text-[var(--color-fonts-font-color-primary)]">{repo.archetypeVersion}</span>
  </span>
)}
```

---

## 3. API Calls to `/upgrades/latest-versions`

**There are none.** No file in `src/` makes any call to `/upgrades/latest-versions` or any `/upgrades/*` endpoint. The only upgrade-related concept is the `upgradeEnabled` boolean field on `RepoSettings`, which is toggled through the existing `PUT /settings/repos/{workspace}/{repoSlug}` endpoint.

---

## 4. Types/Interfaces Related to Archetypes and Versions

Defined in **`src/types/api.ts`**, within the `RepoSettings` interface:

```65:85:src/types/api.ts
export interface RepoSettings {
  id?: number
  workspace: string
  repoSlug: string
  reviewEnabled: boolean
  vectorEnabled: boolean
  docsEnabled: boolean
  upgradeEnabled: boolean
  qualityReportEnabled: boolean
  ruleNames?: string[]
  reviewPrompt?: string
  disabledHooks?: string[]
  confluenceSpaceKey?: string
  confluenceParentPageId?: string
  gitPlatformUrl?: string
  archetype?: string
  archetypeVersion?: string
  archived?: boolean
}
```

Both `archetype` and `archetypeVersion` are **optional strings**. There are no dedicated `ArchetypeVersion` or `LatestVersion` types anywhere in the codebase.

---

## 5. Version Comparison Logic

**There is none.** No semver parsing, no `isOutdated` flag, no comparison between `archetypeVersion` and any latest/target version exists anywhere in the codebase. The version is treated as a pure display value — it is rendered as-is and never evaluated or compared against anything.

---

**Summary**: The codebase currently has minimal archetype/version support — it stores and displays `archetype` and `archetypeVersion` from `RepoSettings` as plain text labels in the Quality Reports and Review Metrics pages. There is no `/upgrades/latest-versions` API call, no dedicated upgrades page, no version comparison logic, and no type definitions beyond the two optional string fields on `RepoSettings`.
